Market stance

The group is defensive and mostly in cash after the S&P's first close below its 200-day in seven months — waiting for capitulation, with NVDA's earnings beat as the one overnight bright spot.

Key watches

Catalysts

  • NVDA earnings beat Tue Nov 17, after close — EPS $2.68 vs $2.47 expected, revenue $115.84B vs $108.71B expected; the first call under interim CEO Colette Kress, with Jensen-return reports in the frame
  • FOMC minutes Wed Nov 18, 2 PM ET — Enrich's watchlist
  • Anthropic IPO pricing reported for today — carried scheduled event
  • Druckenmiller's wall of worry — Remz: Druck tells everyone his net is “low” and he's just shorting copper; Remz thinks he's probably already covered his copper short and been buying all week

Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
Tuesday was another down day and the group reads it as a market to sit out, not to buy. The headline is the 200-day: Remz's SPX chart shows the index closing below its 200-day for the first time in over seven months — 7,344.53 against a 200-day of 7,345 — with a three-month top at 7,560–7,840, the 7,580 retest rejected, invalidated above 7,600, and the June low at 7,150 below. iain agrees on the level and the posture: “likely first close below the 200day, so still no interest in longs until we see capitulation. I'd prefer a quick flush toward June lows, eying ~715, where multiple pivots converge. That'd be my 1st clue of a potential interim bottom, not confirmation.” His charts show the 200-day, the weekly pivot and the March low AVWAP, with VIX spiked into the 27s — he wants VIX 30+ and capitulation before any interim bottom call. Prof warns against calling it: “every time the market looked like it had bottomed, another wave of selling came along. Another bull trap. Another new low.” Enrich is 98%+ cash on cyber headlines and adds only if QQQ holds. Sean posts mindset only — the 80/20 rule, avoiding what made him unprofitable — no tickers, no trades. The one overnight bright spot is NVDA: the first earnings without Jensen beat — EPS $2.68 vs $2.47, revenue $115.84B vs $108.71B — Prof's first-minute candle spiked to 161.32 after hours, and reports swirl of Jensen returning as CEO. Remz's shorts are the trade of the window: opened yesterday, MSTR +187.8%, AMD +104.5%, SKHY +90.8%, DELL +61.3%, CAT +31.4% — AMD still hovers just above his 501 trigger. DiCarlo is the counterweight, calling bottoms on NBIS, IREN and CIFR and MRVL one of the best long-term opportunities — all of them still deep in decline with no base, so the framework treats them as trader calls to watch, not qualifiers. Venu's semiconductor ranking puts the damage in numbers: a median drawdown of −46.4% across 20 chip leaders, 9 of 20 down 50% or more. Your process gives one genuine long qualifier with a trigger above the close (TSLA, compressed on the averages, breakout over 407.46) and one defined short (AMD, under 501.00) — plus AVGO as the contested name, where Enrich's +50% on contracts meets a chart still under every average. The declines, not entries: NVDA at a new 52-week low into the print (now beaten, after hours higher), MSTR at a new 3-month low, and IREN at a new 52-week low. The discipline is in the framing: the indexes lost their 30-week trends and QQQ is under its 50-week EMA too — so the framework says wait for a hold above the triggers, or a pullback into the averages, and tonight's FOMC minutes are the next test.

Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels.
